notes: This slice tracks older consumer GPUs that remain attractive for local LLM inference because their used-market price, VRAM capacity, memory bandwidth, software maturity, or power envelope is still competitive.

Prices are point-in-time Canadian marketplace observations and should not be treated as stable market averages. Shipping, taxes, seller reputation and card condition can materially change effective cost.
Model-size guidance is approximate and assumes quantized inference with additional VRAM reserved for context, KV cache and runtime overhead.
Memory-bandwidth-per-watt and price ratios are coarse hardware economics indicators, not measured LLM throughput or energy-efficiency benchmarks.

hardware.memory_bandwidth_basis: derived from vendor-documented 15 Gbps GDDR6 on a 192-bit bus
hardware.reference_power_connector: 1x 8-pin on many boards; partner implementations vary
hardware.physical_constraints: Common dual-slot cards are roughly 200-305 mm long depending on partner design; compact ITX variants also exist.
software: vLLM ecosystem where model/runtime support permits
hardware.quantization_compatibility: Broad CUDA support for GGUF/llama.cpp and common FP16/BF16, INT8 and INT4 inference paths. Exact GPTQ/AWQ/FP8 kernel support depends on runtime and model architecture; Ampere does not provide Blackwell-era FP4 hardware.
hardware.model_size_practicality: A strong entry card for 7B-8B models at high-quality quantization and many 12B-14B models at Q4-class settings. Larger models normally require partial CPU/system-RAM offload or more aggressive quantization.
hardware.llm_inference_suitability: Still one of the easiest low-cost ways to obtain 12GB of mature CUDA VRAM. Its main limitation is capacity rather than software support.
hardware.performance_per_watt_notes: 360 GB/s at 170W is approximately 2.12 GB/s of memory bandwidth per watt using reference board power.
hardware.off_grid_notes: 170W board power is manageable for a solar-backed desktop, but a complete host will consume materially more. Power limiting can improve energy use at the cost of throughput and should be benchmarked rather than assumed.

pricing.note: Representative pre-owned 12GB RTX 3060 listing observed around CA$370. A separate completed ASUS ROG Strix 12GB listing sold for CA$360 on 2026-08-02, supporting the same approximate used-price band.

hardware.quantization_compatibility: GGUF inference is practical through Vulkan and SYCL-capable llama.cpp builds. XMX-optimized paths can be faster but are more runtime-specific than CUDA. Exact support for model-specific low-bit kernels should be verified against the chosen Intel software stack.
hardware.model_size_practicality: 16GB VRAM is comfortable for many 7B-14B quantized models and gives materially more capacity than 12GB cards. Some 20B-class models can fit only with aggressive quantization and context discipline.
hardware.llm_inference_suitability: A particularly strong used-market capacity/bandwidth value when Intel GPU software is acceptable. Current llama.cpp community usage continues to exercise A770 through Vulkan and SYCL paths, but CUDA remains more universal across AI tooling.
hardware.performance_per_watt_notes: 560 GB/s at 225W is approximately 2.49 GB/s of memory bandwidth per watt using Intel TBP.
hardware.off_grid_notes: 225W TBP is higher than RTX 3060 and newer low-power cards, but the 16GB/560GB/s memory subsystem can justify the draw for bandwidth-bound inference if the host is otherwise efficient.

pricing.note: Representative pre-owned Intel Limited Edition Arc A770 16GB listing observed at CA$397.59. Marketplace prices vary by seller and shipping origin.

software: community HIP/ROCm paths where explicitly verified
hardware.current_rocm_support_status: not listed in AMD's current ROCm 7.2 Radeon PyTorch support matrices; do not assume official ROCm support
hardware.quantization_compatibility: GGUF through llama.cpp Vulkan is the most portable path. Older/community ROCm or HIP configurations may work, but current official Radeon support matrices focus on newer RDNA3/RDNA4 products; treat RX 6800 ROCm compatibility as runtime-specific and unverified unless tested.
hardware.model_size_practicality: 16GB capacity makes many 7B-14B quantized models practical and can accommodate some larger low-bit models with restricted context. The 512GB/s memory subsystem is strong for the observed used price.
hardware.llm_inference_suitability: Attractive as a used Vulkan inference card when 16GB capacity and raw memory bandwidth matter more than official ROCm/PyTorch support. Less turnkey than NVIDIA CUDA and less officially supported for current ROCm than newer Radeon generations.
hardware.performance_per_watt_notes: 512 GB/s at 250W is approximately 2.05 GB/s of memory bandwidth per watt using AMD typical board power.
hardware.off_grid_notes: 250W board power plus a 650W-class recommended PSU makes it less attractive for energy-constrained systems than newer 160-190W cards, although undervolting/power limiting may improve practical efficiency and should be measured per board.

pricing.note: Representative used RX 6800 16GB listing observed at CA$450 plus shipping; other contemporaneous listings were approximately CA$475-499.
